decided_by: Malcolm, 2026-09-10/11, from the standards-photos and eu-lab contact sheets
note:
Malcolm's two picks, both gpt_image:

  std_eu   <- STD-EU-lab-blue-liquid / gpt_image_01     (inspector examining a blue solution)
  std_gmp  <- STD-GMP-inspector-plant / gpt_image_01    (inspector auditing the plant)

ONE ENGINE FOR THE PAIR, WHICH WAS THE DECIDING CRITERION. These two render side by side in the same row, so a split pick wins each picture and loses the pair — the same lesson the skin-repair explainer set cost, except those sat stacked and these sit adjacent, which is less forgiving. Both are gpt_image and share its cool desaturated rendering.

BOTH ARE EXACTLY 2048x1360, so NOTHING NEEDED NORMALISING. That is load-bearing rather than lucky: multi-column renders a block image at its NATURAL aspect ratio, with no wrapper ratio and no object-fit, so two different ratios would have produced two columns of visibly different heights. On both waves nbp_pro and nbp_flash silently returned 4:3 and Luma 16:9 against an explicit 3:2 request, so an nbp or Luma winner would have had to be cropped before it could be used.

THE TWO FIGURES FACE EACH OTHER. The GMP inspector sits right of frame looking left; the EU inspector sits left of centre looking right. std_eu renders in the LEFT column and std_gmp in the RIGHT, so the pair turns inward instead of both staring off the same edge.

BLUE IS THE ONLY COLOUR IN EITHER FRAME — the nitrile gloves in the GMP shot, the gloves and the solution in the EU shot. Everything else in both is graphite, steel and white gowning.

⚠️ flux2 WAS DISCARDED ON BOTH WAVES, on evidence rather than preference: it rendered a legible table of numbered rows on the safety dossier, a marking on the beaker glass, and came back warm-toned against a negated brown ground on all three attempts. That is its documented trait on every glassware wave this project has run.

⚠️ THE ALT TEXT DESCRIBES THE PICTURE AND CLAIMS NOTHING. These are illustrative photographs, not documentation of Skingenetix's own supplier, and on a page about regulatory compliance an image of an inspector sits close to implying it depicts this brand's facility. So neither alt says 'our factory' or 'our laboratory' — they say what is visible and nothing more. Same discipline as the copy above them.

No image is being replaced: both blocks currently have no image at all, so there is no old file to strip and nothing to repoint.
